input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: The wrapper now clears and reuses one shared statistics dict for every call, so overlapping calls to the same decorated function (threads, or recursion) write into and clear the same dict. A call that is still running can have its attempt counts reset mid-retry.
- rationale: Trigger: two threads call the same @retry-decorated function at once, or a decorated function recurses. Mechanism: each call runs stats.clear() on the same dict object that the other in-flight call is updating through copy._local.statistics. Before this change each call had its own dict, so in-flight counts were not reset. Impact: statistics read from an in-progress call (e.g. attempt_number) can be wrong or reset to empty, and the values reported for each call are mixed together.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism: one shared stats dict is cleared and reused on every call, so a concurrent or nested call's stats.clear() wipes the in-flight call's data, including attempt_number, and the statistics get mixed. It also covers the same trigger, overlapping calls from threads or recursion.
